title: Subsecond metering debounce and fair-splitter for streaming token events
creator: Liam Patel
description: Problem: Streaming generation requests emit many partial token events (progress delta messages, interim latencies, retry duplicates, fanout copies to monitoring and billing) which causes noisy real-time meters and frequent downstream overcounts. Symptoms: spikes in tenant usage dashboards during retries, inflated short-window cost alerts, and difficulty producing deterministic per-request cost attribution across multi-route fanout and model-fallback cases. Goal: implement a low-latency debounce + fair-splitter layer that deduplicates subsecond streaming token events, attributes final token counts deterministically to the originating route/model, and produces compact compensated events for the billing pipeline and real-time dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: Streaming events with identical idempotency_key and session_prefix are collapsed within a configurable debounce window (default 300ms) before reaching the billing joiner
When a final terminal event arrives, the system emits a single canonical token-commit event and compensating negative events for any debounced intermediate overcounts

Fair-splitter deterministically assigns tokens for fanout cases across N routes such that the sum of route-attributions equals the canonical token count and ties are resolved by stable hashing of request id

No user-visible billing spikes in 95th percentile for sessions with retries during a 7-day canary run; backfill reconciliation corrects historical duplicates for at least 30 days of late-arriving terminal events
End-to-end integration tests covering retries, partial responses, model-fallbacks, and cross-region fanout pass in CI with deterministic outputs
design_notes: Debounce is implemented as a lightweight streaming stage in the token-ingest Kafka consumer group; it keeps a fixed-size in-memory window keyed by (tenant_id, idempotency_key, session_prefix) and emits when window expires or terminal flag seen
Canonical commit event schema extension: add fields canonical_count, debounced_count, attribution_hash to allow downstream deterministic splitting and compensations

Fair-split algorithm: stable_hash(request_id) mod N to choose primary attribution owner, then proportional split by route_weight for fractional cases; route_weights come from per-tenant routing config in the metadata store

Backfill strategy: run a bounded 'compensation reconciler' batch job that scans terminal events and generates correction events for duplicates within a sliding 30-day window. Job should be idempotent and produce human-readable audit logs for finance
Operational knobs: debounce_window_ms (default 300), max_pending_keys (cap to avoid memory blowup), emit_metrics=true for internal instrumentation
implementation_tasks: Create token-debounce service module (Go) with a Kafka consumer that subscribes to token-progress topic
Schema migration: extend token events topic Avro/Protobuf with canonical_count and attribution_hash (write compat rules in Confluence)
Implement fair-splitter logic and lightweight in-memory shard map; integrate with tenant routing metadata API
Add deterministic compensation event producer to billing topic; ensure correct tombstone handling and exactly-once semantics where possible
Add unit and integration tests that simulate retries, duplicates, terminal-late arrival, and multi-route fanout
Create staged rollout pipeline: shadow mode -> canary (1%)-> regional canary (10%) -> global (100%)
Documentation: update Console docs and runbook with failure modes and mitigation steps
rollout_plan: Week 1: Deploy token-debounce in shadow mode for ingestion of production traffic; metrics recorded to internal dashboard but no writes to billing topic
Week 2: Enable canary write for low-traffic tenant subset and run reconciliation checks nightly
Week 3: Expand regional canary and run compensation backfill for the canary tenants to validate negative event handling
Week 4: Full rollout once 7-day stability criteria met and finance sign-off obtained
monitoring: New Grafana dashboard: debounce.pending_keys, debounce.window_expirations, debounce.eviction_count
Billing health alerts: percent_duplicate_events_by_tenant > 0.5% triggers P1 investigation
SLO: end-to-end billing latency 99th <= 5s for non-backfilled committed events
Audit logs: compensation_job_summary daily with counts of corrected_events and affected_tenants
risks: Memory blow-up if many unique idempotency_key values stream in short bursts; mitigated by max_pending_keys + eviction policy
Ordering guarantees across regions: out-of-order terminal events may cause temporary undercount until reconciler runs
Compensation negative-events may confuse downstream analytics if schema not understood; requires coordinated deploy with analytics
Slight added latency on the ingest path (bounded by debounce_window_ms) could impact customers with sub-100ms real-time dashboards; default window small and configurable per-tenant
